ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, managing partners, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance/Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (CSSF) domestic sanctions measures. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory when any PEP status, adverse media, high-risk third-country nexus, or income tax evasion flags are identified. Screening results must be documented, signed, and retained for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship, pursuant to applicable Luxembourg AML/CFT record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script and must be understandable in at least one of the three Luxembourg administrative languages (Luxembourgish, French, or German). No separate transliteration certificate is required for names using standard Western European Latin characters. The name must not be contrary to public order or morality and must not create confusion with an existing legal entity or trade name. For an SCSp, the name must include the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' as the legal-form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant will receive a written refusal citing the precise statutory ground. The applicant may, within three months of notification, file an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif). For sensitive tokens requiring ministerial approval, the applicant may submit a reasoned request to the competent Minister of Justice and, if refused, appeal that ministerial decision through the same administrative appeal procedure. Alternatively, the applicant may revise the name and resubmit through the LBR/RCS online portal within the existing filing session; no additional fee is charged for the first administrative review within the same pre-incorporation stage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as a correspondence-only address in a low-risk retail e-commerce context, provided that the SCSp maintains a formal registered office in Luxembourg where statutory records, partnership agreements, and registers are accessible to tax authorities, the RCS, and other legally entitled parties. A regulated Luxembourg domiciliation agent or administration company can provide the physical durable address without establishing operational staff premises. However, reliance solely on a virtual office will be considered insufficient substance if the entity engages in significant local management or if tax authorities apply transfer pricing or permanent establishment analysis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: estimated below 10% annual probability for a low-risk standard retail partnership engaged in online FPV drone sales. Unannounced on-site controls are predominantly triggered by filing anomalies, VAT registration mismatches, social security declarations, or AML/CFT alerts rather than by routine oversight. The probability rises to moderate (10–30%) if the SCSp applies for group VAT registration, claims substance-sensitive exemptions, or receives cross-border B2B payments from high-risk jurisdictions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 1, 5, 6-9 (special limited partnerships) and the framework added by the Law of 12 July 2013 on the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Request for registration (demande d'inscription) filed with the RCS together with the signed or notarized partnership agreement and a declaration of conformity
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for the SCSp; capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement, contributions need not be released upfront, and no escrow account is legally required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The General Partner of the SCSp, acting as governing body, hereby: (i) ratifies the subscription to partnership interests by each limited partner at the amounts set forth in the partnership agreement; (ii) adopts the registered office at [street, postcode] Luxembourg City; (iii) appoints [Name] as managing General Partner's representative and [Name] as accountable officer with exclusive day-to-day authority over the SCSp's affairs; (iv) instructs the officers to complete RCS registration, RESA publication, tax filings, and bank account opening; (v) confirms that no Shares are issued and that partner capital is released only when agreed. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutive meeting and execution of SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary in Luxembourg (if notarized); alternatively private writing with subsequent RCS filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Parties execute the partnership agreement, specifying object, contributions, profit-sharing, management powers, and registered office. If notarized, the notary handles signature and coordinates authentication. Provide original or certified copy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected by the notary or parties, amend the act and re-execute; no cure needed for private writing except correcting errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS; online via lbr.lu or in person at the Luxembourg City branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration request and accompanying documents through the LBR online filing portal or at the registry. The registrar verifies the existence of the legal form, statutory requirements, and registered office address. Pay any applicable fee.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement (original or notarized copy)
Declaration de conformité signed by the general partner
Identity documents of partners and general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a deficit note, correct the deficiencies within 3 months; file rectifying declaration or acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The LBR transmits the registration text to the electronic official gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA). The publication is mandatory for third-party effectiveness.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or supplement in RESA by filing a corrective notice; cost is minor administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg tax administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, submit the VAT registration form (Formulaire 2014) and, if required, tax registration. The AEDT allocates a VAT number for Luxembourg and EU transactions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, provide missing items; if non-resident partners are involved, confirm permanent establishment status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – SME and Crafts Department (Middle Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application online via guichet.lu or on paper with proof of professional qualification. The authorization covers industrial operations and retail sale of drones. The permit must be obtained before trading.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file appeal with the Grand-Ducal administrative court; alternatively, narrow the activity scope and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental and fire safety license/clearance for workshop operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement (AEnv); Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an environmental permit if the workshop qualifies as a class 2 installation; obtain fire safety certificate after inspection. Work is allowed provisionally only after clearance.
required_dossiers: Proof of insurance and building approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deficiencies are identified, submit a remediation plan; administrative appeal with AEnv within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs and Crafts, under the Law of 2 September 2011; municipal authorities for land-use and building permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (establishment permit) covering manufacturing and retail, plus a communal operating permit (autorisation d'exploitation) for the machining and assembly workshop

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (AEnv) – Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (class 2) – small-scale CNC milling and brushless motor assembly; full EIA report not mandatory
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Luxembourg water law (Law of 22 July 2012) and municipal discharge limits; VOCs and solvent emissions: EU Directive 2004/42/EC as transposed; airborne carbon-fiber dust: occupational exposure limit for respirable dust (2.5 mg/m³) with local exhaust ventilation; waste handling: separate collection of hazardous composite waste under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); structural load certification by an approved engineer; occupational health and workplace inspection clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; portal: myguichet.lu / e-TVA / eCDF
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign taxable person (including an SCSp treated as an independent taxable person for VAT) must register for Luxembourg VAT if it carries out any taxable transaction. File VAT registration Form 1 (normal) or Form 2 (small business exemption) via MyGuichet.lu or in paper form with AEDT; non-established EU/third-country persons may be required to appoint a fiscal representative in specific cases. The Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA) is issued upon registration; no separate income tax ID is required for a transparent SCSp for entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Article 175bis LIR election for partnerships to be taxed as corporations; VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') election; no US-style check-the-box; ATAD hybrid mismatch rules apply with anti-abuse safeguards.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for domestic small business exemption; EUR 10,000 intra-EU distance sales threshold; no turnover threshold for non-established taxable persons (any taxable supply triggers registration obligation)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or CTC (continuous transaction control) regime exists; e-invoicing is permitted, and B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for public contracts using Peppol/UBL formats; no digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to non-EU third countries are zero-rated provided the supplier holds adequate proof of export (delivery outside the EU and documentary evidence); intra-EU supplies are zero-rated if the customer's valid EU VAT ID is obtained and EC sales listings are submitted; B2B services supplied to non-established businesses may be zero-rated under reverse-charge/place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport/documentary evidence (B/L, CMR, airway bill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (where required to substantiate forex repatriation / export proceeds)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated export zero-rating triggers retrospective VAT reassessment (clawback) within the statutory limitation period (extended to 10 years in case of fraud). Late payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month. Administrative fines up to 20% of the tax due (or 100% for intentional fraud, up to EUR 250,000) and criminal penalties apply for fraudulent zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank and balance-of-payments reporting authority, acting within the European Central Bank (ECB) and Eurosystem framework; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises payment institutions, electronic money institutions and AML/CTF compliance for credit and financial entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full euro-area member and applies unconditional convertibility on both current-account and capital-account operations by virtue of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-66 TFEU). The euro is a fully convertible reserve currency; there are no exchange-control approvals, no conversion ceilings, no prior licensing for profit remittance, partner capital subscriptions, loan repayments, or liquidation distributions of a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp). The operative practical hurdles are limited to: (i) mandatory BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border fund transfers when the monthly aggregated amount exceeds EUR 12,500 per counterparty or transaction; (ii) mandatory payer and payee identity data attached to every SWIFT MT103 or SEPA transfer under the EU Wire Transfer Regulation (EU) 2015/847, with enhanced identity verification for transfers exceeding EUR 1,000; and (iii) a current and accurate file at the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) identifying the natural persons behind the limited partners. The SCSp is tax-transparent; profit remittances and partner withdrawals are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the partnership level, and non-resident partners are not taxed in Luxembourg on distributions to the extent no Luxembourg permanent establishment is created. Full profit-repatriation freedom extends to non-EEA OECD and non-OECD counterparties subject only to EU sanctions screening and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no compulsory repatriation or retention-period regime in Luxembourg. Export receipts generated from global sales of FPV racing drones, including PayPal/Stripe card settlements, SWIFT corporate transfers and letter-of-credit disbursements, may be freely held in euro or any foreign currency, converted at any time, or placed on interest-bearing accounts at Luxembourg or foreign financial institutions. The only compliance duties are: (i) monthly BCL balance-of-payments statistical filing by the resident exporter when aggregated cross-border receipts exceed EUR 12,500; (ii) EU customs-archive obligations requiring export declarations, commercial invoices, and air waybills to be kept for at least five years; and (iii) standard corporate record retention for VAT and CIT audit purposes. No Central Bank permission is needed to open a foreign-currency account or to utilise the proceeds overseas.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account with partner-capital sub-ledger (escrow-ready)
Operational Account combined with Trade Finance and Commercial Letter of Credit facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Spuerkeess / Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and FX / Treasury Hedging Account
Digital-first Settlement Account for PayPal/Stripe e-commerce float

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for payment collection and disbursement: European-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions (Wise Europe, Airwallex, Revolut Business, PayPal Luxembourg S.à r.l., Stripe operating under the Luxembourg or Irish passporting regime) are legally available rails for the SCSp because they act under Directive 2009/110/EC and revised PSD2, passported to Luxembourg and supervised by the CSSF or the home-state competent authority. Feasibility rating: High for FX conversion, supplier disbursements, mass payouts and e-commerce settlement; Medium for multi-currency treasury floats because EMI client-money protection and segregation rules are less complete than the prudential protections of a systemic credit institution; Low for capital escrow, documentary trade transactions, commercial letters of credit and bank guarantees, which must remain with a tier-1 credit institution. The recommended architecture is a primary relationship with a tier-1 Luxembourg bank for capital escrow and trade finance, with EMIs attached as pass-through collection and settlement sub-ledgers only. Use of an unlicensed offshore EMI outside the EEA is not advisable and would create a serious AML/CTF compliance blocker for the Luxembourg banking group.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg statutes do not impose a mandatory physical appearance for corporate account opening; CSSF guidance and Circular 20/744 permit remote video identification with qualified electronic signatures for lower-risk partnerships. In practice, tier-1 banks accept remote onboarding for a Low_Risk_Standard FPV drone retail business only when the gérant (general partner) and every beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the SCSp complete automated identity verification and a recorded live video interview with the bank's compliance officer; the Luxembourg registered office, the partner structure, and the RBE excerpt must be independently verifiable. BGL BNP Paribas and BIL, as the most conservative institutions, may additionally require one physical onboarding meeting in Luxembourg City for the authorised signatory or a notarially certified copy of the partnership agreement and the gérant appointment, with apostille and sworn translation for documents originating in non-French or non-German-speaking jurisdictions. The SCSp does not have directors in the corporate sense; the gérant acts as manager and must be identified in the account mandate. Plan for one virtual interview with a possible physical fallback; realistic onboarding lead time is three to six weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain through a Luxembourg SCSp with non-EU limited partners, triggering mandatory look-through to ultimate natural persons under the Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019 implementing the Fifth Money Laundering Directive.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE registration certificate; complete ownership-chain chart to natural persons; passport copies and residential addresses of all partners above the 25% threshold; source-of-funds declarations for each capital contribution; bank statements evidencing the historical origin of subscription funds; tax-residency certificates of partners; and a written commercial memorandum explaining each partner's role in the FPV drone manufacturing and retail activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and shell-risk: the SCSp is perceived as a letterbox vehicle with no premises, no activity and no operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg registered-office contract; signed agreements with a local carbon-fibre milling subcontractor or co-manufacturer; evidence of warehouse or third-party logistics capacity; management accounts prepared by a Luxembourg-certified accountant; purchase orders from Asian component suppliers; distributor and B2B contracts for racing drones; marketing spend and e-commerce order data; and a written substance report from the local fiduciary describing premises, decision-making locus, operational management and economic risk-bearing of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk settlement corridors: frequent wire traffic from Hong Kong, Singapore and mainland Chinese suppliers combined with PayPal/Stripe consumer chargebacks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, air waybills and bills of lading; Incoterms and purchase agreements; vendor KYC questionnaires; EU customs declarations under HS 3926 and HS 8501 for carbon-fibre components and brushless motors; full payment-history explanations; OFAC/EU consolidated sanctions and PEP screening outputs; and a written supply-chain narrative proving legitimate cross-border trade in racing-drone components.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-velocity card receipts: thousands of low-value PayPal/Stripe transactions entering a newly opened partnership account without robust merchant compliance controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal (Luxembourg) and Stripe merchant agreements in the SCSp name; PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation; 3-D Secure 2.0 configuration evidence; refund, dispute and chargeback management policy; EU consumer-terms and privacy policy; product-liability insurance covering carbon-fibre drone sales; and analytical summaries distinguishing genuine cross-border e-commerce revenue from card testing or fraud.rt

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-licence ambiguity: compliance risk that the bank or regulators classify FPV racing-drone manufacturing as an aviation, weapons, or dual-use business requiring special authorisations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Classification letter from the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy confirming ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 sports-goods and toy/game manufacturing status; confirmation that no financial-services licence is required since the payment rails are operated by regulated PSPs and EMIs; an EASA / OPS Regulation (EU) 2019/947 operational-assignment letter for end consumers; and a dual-use and export-control statement confirming the absence of ITAR, EAR or EU dual-use list items in the FPV drone components.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for partner capital subscriptions: (1) each partner remits funds exclusively by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer from a financial institution in the partner's own name directly to the SCSp IBAN (LU-prefix account at a Luxembourg bank); (2) under Regulation (EU) 2015/847, all transfers must carry full payer and payee identity, and the receiving bank must verify the payer's identity when the transaction exceeds EUR 1,000; (3) where the monthly aggregate cross-border flow exceeds EUR 12,500, the receiving bank files the BCL balance-of-payments declaration under the direct-investment equity category (SCSp participating interests); (4) the compliance dossier must contain the signed partnership subscription deed, the updated RBE extract showing the capital increase, the gérant resolution accepting the contribution, and a source-of-funds statement for each remittance; (5) non-euro contributions are converted at the bank's spot rate on the value date, with the FX conversion contract retained in the treasury file; (6) banks may place a two-business-day provisional-credit hold pending validation of the origin and purpose; (7) no Luxembourg capital duty applies to SCSp capital contributions (the old droit d'apport was abolished in 2019; a flat EUR 25 registration fee may apply to the notarisation of the partnership deed if filed with the Business Registers); (8) forbidden routing includes unhosted cryptocurrency transfers, promissory-note assignments, or transit through opaque offshore trust vehicles, all of which would be treated as material AML red flags and could trigger a frozen account and a suspicious-transaction report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro-denominated suppliers within SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer with near-real-time settlement. For Asian carbon-fibre and brushless-motor manufacturers, the standard rails are SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers with a goods-payment description matching the invoiced purchase order, or an irrevocable sight Commercial Letter of Credit opened by BGL BNP Paribas or BIL and confirmed by the beneficiary bank in Hong Kong or mainland China. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are an acceptable lower-cost alternative once the trade relationship matures. For distributor rebates and dropship payments, use the bank's Bank Payment Undertaking (BPU) facility or the PayPal/Stripe mass-payout API funded from the ING or BIL settlement sub-ledger. Every disbursement above EUR 10,000 should require dual signature authorisation, an order-reference mark, and confirmation by the bank that the payee passes EU and OFAC sanctions screening. All outbound monies paid for imported goods must be matched against the EU customs declaration to permit VAT and BOP reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/CNH deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with tenors of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, executed under an ISDA or EMTA-style master agreement confirmed by the LC-issuing bank's treasury front office

EUR/CNH Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing the offshore CNH fixing rate, permissible for hedging mainland-China supplier costs where physical CNY delivery is unavailable to a non-resident entity
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps for the structural conversion of capital-escrow base into the trade-payment currency envelope

FX collar and participating-forward structures permitted as OTC option strategies, provided the bank confirms the SCSp's underlying trade exposure and the structure carries no speculative or leveraged proprietary element
Spot-for-forward rebalancing hedges settled through SWIFT MT300 FX confirmations and reconciled monthly by the external treasury advisor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing (RBE annual recertification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the accounting year-end; for a non-calendar SCSp financial year, within three months of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing is a criminal offence: up to EUR 250,000 fine for the entity, EUR 125,000 for officers, plus publication of the non-compliant status; repeated failure may lead to RCS deregistration action and banking relationship disruption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax declaration (Form 700 and integrated municipal business-tax assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the year following the 31 December tax year; e-filed returns currently receive an administrative extension to 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 1,000 per return, late-payment interest of 0.8% per month on assessed tax, and forced assessment when no return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts/balance-sheet deposit with RCS (exemption for transparent SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual filing is due for a standard SCSp without separate legal personality; if an exception applies, the filing must occur within seven months of the financial year-end and before the one-month-after-approval deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not applicable in the default exemption; in an exception case, late or omitted deposit triggers administrative penalties up to EUR 5,000 and potential publication of the default judgment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if the SCSp elects for the annual VAT filing regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return for a calendar-year taxpayer is due on 31 March of the following year; standard monthly/quarterly VAT returns remain the default for ongoing commercial sales of FPV drone products.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment incurs default interest and administrative penalties up to 10% of VAT due; wilful omission is criminalised and may trigger fines up to EUR 125,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent audit is statutorily required for a transparent SCSp below the Luxembourg large-undertaking thresholds. An audit becomes mandatory only if two of the three following indicators are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50; additional group-audit obligations may arise under the parent-companies law if the SCSp belongs to a consolidated group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended, and the Plan comptable luxembourgeois) applies to bookkeeping records; IFRS is optional for voluntary or group consolidated statements and is not required for a standalone SCSp.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually confirm in the RBE register that the declared beneficial owners, direct or indirect ownership percentages, voting rights, and control paths are unchanged, or must submit an amendment within one month of any change. The annual confirmation is made on or before 31 March following the accounting year-end. The general partner is responsible for filing and must keep a documented evidence file for each confirmation.

Register of General Partners and Appointment Resolutions
